A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same continuous simplicial neural network, renamed from COSMOS to COSIMO. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original trajectory-prediction and shape-regression results, plus stability, over-smoothing, and branch-count experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those results and adds node-classification, graph-classification, and runtime/memory measurements.

M1.justification: The PDEs, exponential Hodge filters, network layer, branch aggregation, and truncated spectral implementation are retained. Remark 5.6 explicitly documents learnable diffusion times, without establishing a change to the earlier procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds node classification on high-school and senate-bills and graph classification on proteins. These introduce new prediction tasks and domains beyond the retained trajectory and partial-shape evaluations.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds evaluated comparisons with GCN, GraphSAGE, GIN, GAT, SaNN, and GSAN, alongside retained comparators SCCNN and SAN. The original trajectory and shape comparator sets remain unchanged; PSNN becoming SCoNe in Table 1 matches the same cited work and results.

E3.justification: The new classification evaluations introduce chronological 80/20 partitions for high-school and senate-bills and ten stratified folds for proteins. Appendix I adds runtime and GPU-memory evaluation on Shrec-16. The stated settings of retained experiments remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix I examines the runtime–memory–prediction-error tradeoff on both Shrec-16 variants. The noise-stability, over-smoothing, effective-depth, and branch-count analyses are retained, including material relocated to Appendices M and N.

E5.justification: v2 introduces accuracy averaging over ten stratified folds for the new graph-classification evaluation. The original 30-, 50-, and 100-realization analyses and existing uncertainty-reporting conventions are retained. Table 1's rescaled and rounded uncertainties do not establish changed statistical procedures.

E6.justification: New Table 3 reports COSIMO accuracies of 0.90 ± 0.05, 0.69 ± 0.08, and 0.79 ± 0.01 on high-school, senate-bills, and proteins, respectively, plus comparator results and GSAN's senate-bills OOM outcome. Figure 5 adds resource measurements. Original benchmark results and analysis curves are retained; Table 1 only changes units and rounding.

T1.justification: Theorem 5.3 gains a factor s in its first bound term, comparing v1 Equation 21 with v2 Equation 15, aligning the statement with the existing Appendix F derivation. Other theoretical results are retained; separating existing proof inequalities into numbered displays is primarily presentation.

C1.justification: The novelty, stability, and over-smoothing-control claims remain intact. The conclusion extends its empirical superiority claim to node and graph classification, broadening the claimed application scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations linking classification performance to higher-order information and discusses the measured efficiency tradeoff. Its conclusion newly identifies dependence on eigendecomposition and possible alternatives. The earlier over-squashing caveat remains, relocated to Appendix M.

D1.justification: v2 adds an A100 GPU with 40 GB memory disclosure, node-dataset simplex counts, and an explicit statement about learning diffusion times. It drops v1's description of the 76 original TOSCA shapes. Detailed hyperparameters remain deferred to supplementary code.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations including GRAND, GraphSAGE, SaNN, generalized simplicial attention, DiffusionNet, and the node-dataset source, while removing the TOSCA-related book citation. The central positioning against discrete SCCNNs remains unchanged; publication updates and the duplicated GAT reference are not new research coverage.

P1.justification: The revision edits exposition throughout the introduction, related work, and methods; reorganizes experimental subsections; and moves implementation details, dataset descriptions, and a limitation into appendices. It also renames the model throughout and revises the title and conclusion heading.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is substantially redrawn to visualize evolving lower, upper, and joint dynamics. v2 adds Tables 3–4 and the efficiency Figure 5, places Tables 1–2 side by side, resizes and relocates existing figures, and reorganizes proof displays. Minor defects include 'Table??' and a 'SAT' plot label versus 'SAN' in Table 2.

improvement.justification: The new classification comparisons and measured resource tradeoffs address v1's narrow application validation and lack of empirical cost evidence, substantially strengthening assessment of the model's usefulness. The theorem correction and redesigned schematic improve consistency and clarity. Experimental details remain limited and minor labeling defects appear, but these do not outweigh the substantive gains.
